The line segment $\overline{AB}$ is shown below. Find $\overline{A'B'},$ the image of $\overline{AB}$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14056071/assets/2e22400d15abc81150d6d18de591549e81a46bd16ab9e95f10f86bae2125b490.png)
e-6682.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overline{AB}$ under the action of $\mathbf T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overline{AB}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14056071/assets/fe82a0c8616e43c9d8db0b2892a145fcabf4cfa17bd3d4e033a1349cd25921ee.png)

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are $A'(1,3)$ and $B'(1,-2),$ as shown below.

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(1,-2)$ and $B(-2,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(-1,-4)$ and ${B}^{′}(-1,-1).$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Segment Under the Action of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(1,-2)$ and $B(-2,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(-1,-4)$ and ${B}^{′}(-1,-1).$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(1,1)$ and $B(-1,2).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(2,2)$ and ${B}^{′}(-5,7).$

content.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(2,3)$ and $B(1,-2).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(2,1)$ and ${B}^{′}(1,-3).$
